"The power grid security management system of 2025."
Power grid safety management system
Section 1 Power grid security management system
Chapter I General provisions
In order to strengthen the safety of the electricity grid, ensure the safe and stable operation of the electricity system, and guarantee the population ' s needs for electricity, including for life, production and defence research, the system is established in accordance with the Law of the People ' s Republic of China on Electricity and the Regulations on the Protection of Electrical Facilities.
Article II. This system applies to electricity production enterprises, grid-operated enterprises, electricity users and other relevant units and individuals in our country.
Article 3 Safety management of the grid should be guided by the principles of safety first, prevention, integrated management and continuous improvement, ensuring the safe, reliable and efficient operation of the power system.
Article 4 Power enterprises should establish a sound grid safety management system, with clear responsibilities, enhanced training, improved personnel quality and effective implementation of the grid safety management system.
Chapter II Power Net Safety Management Organization
Article 5 Power enterprises shall establish grid safety management bodies responsible for organizing, coordinating and supervising grid safety management.
Article 6. Key responsibilities of the power grid safety authority:
(i) Organization and improvement of the grid safety management system;
(ii) Organize the development of grid safety development plans and annual work plans;
(iii) Organization of grid safety risk assessments and emergency response

"The power grid security management system of 2025."
Article 11 Power enterprises shall establish a well-established network movement management system and strictly enforce the movement control instructions to ensure the safe and stable operation of the power system.
Article 12 Power enterprises should strengthen the management of the operation and maintenance of grid equipment, and should conduct regular inspections, tests and maintenance to ensure the safe and reliable operation of the equipment.
Article 13 Power enterprises should strengthen the security management of information in the grid and establish a sound information security protection system to prevent information from being leaked, tampered with and destroyed.
Chapter V Security management of grid construction
Article 14 Power enterprises should establish a secure management system for grid-building and ensure that it is built safely.
Article 15 Power enterprises should strictly enforce safety protocols and standards in the construction of the grid and strengthen the security supervision of construction sites.
Article 16 - Power enterprises should strengthen the management of the completion and delivery of grid construction projects to ensure that they meet safety requirements.
Chapter VI. Power grid safety response
Article 17 Power enterprises should establish a well-established grid safety incident management mechanism to ensure that accidents are dealt with in a timely and effective manner.
Article 18 Emergency preparedness should be activated immediately in the event of an accident in an electrical company, measures should be taken to prevent the accident from spreading, accident investigation and analysis should be organized and corrective measures proposed

"The power grid security management system of 2025."
Article 18 In the event of a security accident in an electrical utility, the emergency plan shall be immediately activated, measures taken to prevent the accident from spreading, accident investigation and analysis organized and corrective measures proposed.
Article 19 Power enterprises should regularly summarize safety incidents, analyse the causes of accidents, strengthen safety management and prevent the recurrence of similar accidents.
Chapter VII Training and awareness-raising on grid safety
Article 20 - Power enterprises should strengthen grid safety training and awareness-raising and promote safety awareness and safety skills for their employees.
Article 21 Electricity enterprises shall organize regular training in grid safety to ensure that employees have the necessary safety knowledge and skills.
Article 22 Power enterprises should conduct grid safety awareness education through various channels to raise public awareness of safety.
Chapter VIII. Legal responsibility and appraisal
Article 23 Power enterprises shall perform their duties in accordance with the law in connection with the safety of the grid, in violation of the regime and shall be liable accordingly under the law.
Article 24 Power enterprises should establish a system for the safety of the grid, which should be applied to units and individuals who fail to perform safety management duties.
Annex IX
Article 25 The system shall prevail over any provisions of the former relevant provisions which are incompatible with the system from the date of their issuance.
Article 26

"Air Quality Management Scheme."
Air quality management approach
General provisions
(i) Purpose
This approach is designed to strengthen air quality management, ensure that air quality meets relevant standards, protect public health and promote sustainable economic and social development.
(ii) Scope of application
This approach applies to the management of air emission sources in the course of the company/organization operations, including, but not limited to, production workshops, office areas, storage facilities, etc., where waste is generated.
(iii) Basic principles
1. In accordance with the principles of the law: strict compliance with national and local laws and regulations on air quality and industry standards, ensuring that air pollutants are released in accordance with the requirements.
2. The principle of prevention is the dominant principle: strengthening source controls, taking effective measures to prevent and reduce the generation of air pollutants and reducing the impact on air quality from the source.
3. Principles of process management: To manage the entire process of planning, designing, building, operating and maintaining air emission sources and ensure that air quality management measures are in place for all stages.
4. Principle of continuous improvement: Continuous optimization of air quality management measures, continuous improvement of air quality, adaptation to environmental requirements and corporate/organizational development.

"Notification by the Ministry of Transport of the issuance of the Safety Risk Assessment Guidelines for Construction of High-Stamp Highways Project (on a trial basis)
Ministry of Transport circular on the issuance of safety risk assessment guidelines for the construction of highway high slope works (pilot)
Hand over to DAWN 266 (2014)
The departments of the provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government and the Military and Military Construction Corps of Xinjiang (the Directorate and the Commission):
To improve the safety risk system for highway construction, enhance safety risk management for roadside works, improve the dedicated construction programme and enhance safety risk preparedness at construction sites, the Ministry has organized the development of the Safety Risk Assessment Guide for highway high slope works (pilot) which is now being published and implemented as of 1 March 2015.
In order to regulate the work on the construction safety risk assessment, the following requirements are made:
1. Any new, modified or expanded highways included in national and local capital plans shall be subject to a safety risk assessment of the construction of high road slopes during the construction phase.
II. Due attention should be paid to the adverse geological areas such as old landslides, rock piles, old fallers, special rocky areas such as swelling earth, high liquid limit soil, frozen soil, yellow soil, and residential areas, underground pipe distribution, high pressure towers

"Notification by the Ministry of Transport of the issuance of the Safety Risk Assessment Guidelines for Construction of High-Stamp Highways Project (on a trial basis)
(c) Safety risk assessment of construction of special rock plots such as scalding, high liquid limit, tundra, yellow soil, and surrounding areas such as residential areas, underground pipe distribution areas, high pressure towers, etc.
The risk assessment for the safety of construction works on the high slopes of highway roads is divided into two phases: a general risk assessment and a specific risk assessment.
(i) Overall risk assessment. The overall roadside engineering for the highway is assessed as a whole, assessing safety risks, determining risk levels and recommending control measures for the construction of the roadside slopes, depending on the scale of the construction, geological conditions, engineering characteristics, construction environment, trigger factors, data integrity, etc. The overall risk assessment should be used as the basis for the preparation of the construction organization design for the roadside slopes.
(ii) Ad hoc risk assessments. Based on the overall risk assessment, the road segments of the risk class up to the high risk level (level III) and above are used as assessment modules, which are targeted at construction operations and are identified, analysed and estimated according to their construction safety risk characteristics and similar engineering accidents; and a quantitative assessment of the significant risk sources and specific risk control measures are proposed.

"Notification by the Ministry of Transport of the issuance of the Safety Risk Assessment Guidelines for Construction of High-Stamp Highways Project (on a trial basis)
The risk assessment can be divided into pre-construction and ad hoc evaluations of the construction process. The risk assessment should serve as a basis for developing or refining the dedicated construction programme.
The specific assessment methodology may be selected by reference to the Safety Risk Assessment Guide for Construction of High-Stamps on Highway Roads ( Trial).
The risk assessment shall be completed before the construction of the sub-project on the roadside.
Evaluation of the organization and evaluation report.
(i) The overall risk assessment is organized by the construction unit, which is responsible for the ad hoc risk assessment. The organizational unit is responsible for the quality of the assessment, in accordance with the principle of “who organizes who is responsible”.
(ii) General and pre-construction risk assessments should be assessed

"Notification by the Ministry of Transport of the issuance of the Safety Risk Assessment Guidelines for Construction of High-Stamp Highways Project (on a trial basis)
Organizational units are responsible for the quality of the assessment, in accordance with the principle of “whose organization is responsible”.
(ii) The overall risk assessment and the pre-construction risk assessment shall form separate assessments, and the ad hoc risk assessment of the construction process may streamline the form of the assessment statement. The assessment report shall reflect the full scope of the risk assessment process and shall include such aspects as the basis for preparation, engineering profile, assessment methodology, assessment steps, assessment content, assessment findings and response recommendations.
VII. Implementation requirements.
(i) If a highway project is to commence after 1 March 2015, an overall project risk assessment shall be organized.
(ii) The construction unit shall, based on the findings of the risk assessment, refine the design of the construction organization and the special construction programme for the high slopes of the road, classify the corresponding ad hoc contingency plans and implement early warning control of the project ' s construction process. A system of daily inspection, monitoring of early warning, periodic reports, sales numbers, etc. for major sources of risk should be established and strictly enforced.
(iii) Safety risk assessment work on highway high slope works in project

The measures should be immediately discontinued for level IV risks.
(iii) The cost of the safety risk assessment for the construction of the high slopes of highway roads is charged to the project ' s safe production costs.
(iv) Provincial transport authorities and their regulatory agencies should incorporate into their inspection the implementation of the safety risk assessment for construction on highways high slopes, in the performance of their duties of supervision and inspection of construction safety.
The implementation of the Safety Risk Assessment Guidelines for the Construction of High-Stamps on Highway Roadways should be actively promoted at all locations, and the problems and recommendations identified in the assessment should be communicated to the Department ' s Safety and Quality Oversight Management Division in a timely manner for revision and refinement.

I. SUMMARY OF WORK
(i) Mission source.
In recent years, the construction of our road tunnel has been developing rapidly, the tunnel works have been moving in the direction of deep burial and growth, the geological conditions of the tunnel works, construction conditions are more complex, and operational safety risks are more pronounced. To strengthen the security risk management management of the tunnel works, effective protection against safety accidents, it is necessary to carry out a safety risk assessment of the tunnel works during the construction phase, increase risk management awareness, optimize the construction programme, and improve the security risk identification and control capabilities of the construction works.

Scope
The tunnel construction is a high-risk industry, and the tunnel security accident has been characterized by “expensive, frequent, multi-pattern” for many years, owing to the complexity of the environment, poor construction conditions, rapid changes in the dynamics of insecurity, complex security incidents and the mobility of the main players [1]. The complex geologic conditions of the various regions of the country are becoming increasingly evident, the construction of tunnels is facing serious challenges, and the safety assessment of the tunnel construction is essential to ensuring the safety and quality of the tunnel construction; low-risk tunnel works do not require or require simple risk control measures; and high-risk tunnels require complex and effective risk management measures to reduce the risks to acceptable ranges.
The standards set out the basic principles for the risk assessment of the safety of the construction of the tunnel works, including the delineation of the assessment phase

"Guide to risk assessment for road works, part 3: tunnel works."
Risk is reduced to an acceptable range.
The criteria set out the basic principles for the assessment of safety risks for the construction of tunnel works, including the delineation of the assessment phase, the selection of the assessment methodology and the assessment of the implementation steps.
The assessment phase consists mainly of a general risk assessment and a specific risk assessment. The overall risk assessment is a comprehensive assessment of the risks involved in the construction of the tunnel works prior to the start of the project, which provides decision support for the allocation of resources, such as personnel and equipment, the decision to undertake a dedicated risk assessment, the preliminary identification of major risk sources, etc. The specific risk assessment is a quantitative assessment of the risks associated with the loss of the hole in the construction areas of the tunnel works, collapse, silt, deformation, gas explosion, rock explosion, etc. For the overall risk assessment, a simple operational, practical system of indicators and assessment methods should be proposed, highlighting their practicality; and for the specific risk assessment, scientific and dynamic aspects should be highlighted.
The method of construction of road tunnels is mainly the drill method, the TBM method, the sunk method, etc. Although the TBM method, the sunk method, may be applied to the construction of tunnels in complex rock conditions, the drill method

Therefore, the standard is mainly based on drilling works, which are applied to new road tunnels with the primary means of excavation, and the construction safety risk assessment of the construction of the remodel and expansion of road tunnels can be used in conjunction with other types of tunnels. In addition, the criteria for overall risk classification in the risk assessment, the type of risk-assessments and the possible classification criteria for each risk-related event and the possibility of classification of the tests are mainly determined by statistical analysis of the relevant engineering cases, and the risk of tunnels that are beyond their scope should be further studied.

The risk estimation recommended methodology for general and significant risk sources is mentioned in the risk estimation section, but the relationship between general and significant risk sources is not indicated, resulting in part of the risk estimation being less logical and the terms of reference for establishing risk estimates are more divergent.
After an in-depth study of the risk assessment process, the team conducted several workshops in which it was decided to include risk estimates, general risk source estimates, risk source estimates for significant risks, and three subsections of the risk assessment. The general principles of risk estimation are described in the risk estimates and identified as significant.

"Guide to risk assessment for road works, part 3: tunnel works."
The risk estimation describes the general principles underlying the risk estimation and indicates that the source of significant risk is generated by general risk source estimation; the general risk source risk estimation and the risk source risk estimation specify the estimation of general and significant risk sources, respectively. Through the structure above, the relationship between general risk sources and significant risk sources is clarified, and the risk estimation is partly logical and process-specific.
2. Methods for assessing the severity of the consequences of significant risk events in a specific risk assessment:
The gravity of the consequences of risk events in the current guidelines is primarily considered for human casualties and direct economic loss, and the high principle is used to determine that the standard introduces a consequence equivalence approach that combines the consequences of human casualties, direct economic loss, social impact, environmental impact, and delay in the construction of the work schedule.
Consider the principle of high standards (persons) as a rule.

The criteria for converting results are valid and tested on that basis. Considering that the method of determining consequences in relation to the high principle (taking into account both consequences of human casualties and direct economic loss) is generally retained, it is appropriate to use the consequence-equivalency approach to determine the severity of the risk event when multiple consequences occur.

6.1 Purpose

6.2 Time of implementation
The company should concentrate on the first course of safe production starting every spring day of work, whether or not it is suspended.
